blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The findings of a new international study challenge the familiar belief that corporal punishment produces more disciplined children, with the lead researcher in the Philippines pointing out that preventing school violence depends on addressing children’s relationships at home and in school. Dr. Liane Peña Alampay of Ateneo de Manila University said in an Ateneo Breakthroughs discussion that more frequent spanking is linked to greater anxiety and aggression in children over time, stressing that “in no instance does corporal punishment have positive effects.” Alampay drew from the Parenting Across Cultures (PAC) research initiative, described as the largest multicultural and […]...
